newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian rugby union chief executive John O'Neill believes the next coach of the national team should have a guaranteed three-year appointment instead of the current two-year contract. Speculation over the future of current coach Greg Smith is mounting and many critics believe he will be replaced by ACT Brumbies coach Rod Macqueen within a few months. Page 47.

A new sponsorship deal has guaranteed the future of Bathurst's new Holden against Ford V8 1000 kilometre endurance motor race. American telecommunications company Primus has been signed as a four-year multi-million dollar sponsor to the race, of which the inaugural meeting was held last year. Page 47.

Two potential weightlifting medallists have migrated from Armenia to Australia and will compete in the Victorian championships next month. Australian Weightlifting Federation president Sam Coffa said the defections will significantly boost Australia's chnces in two weight classes. Page 47.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian rugby union side may be unchanged for the Test against New Zealand in Dunedin on August 16. After each Test this year, and throughout the reign of coach Greg Smith, the side has been regularly changed, and to keep the same side for consecutive games would be a rarity. Matthew Burke may be the only omission through injury. Page 48.

The Australian Rugby League is likely to offer Super League financial control of a merged competition in return for overall control of the game. Representatives from both competitions will meet today in an attempt to progress peace talks. Page 47.

The Canberra and Penrith club rugby union premiership teams may be retained in next year's competition, despite earlier predictions. The union's first division presidents voted on Monday to ensure that all current 14 teams remain for next year, despite a statute specifying that only 12 teams should compete in 1998. Page 47.
THE AGE

Essendon Australian Football League player Che Cockatoo-Collins may return to his home city of Adelaide to play for Port Power. If Port is successful in obtaining his brothers Donald and David in a trade, Cockatoo-Collins has expressed his wish to join the team. Page B16.

The Australian under-23 men's basketball team is likely to qualify for the championship quarter-finals despite losing to Argentina in Melbourne last night 81-67. The team is likely to play either Puerto Rico or the United States in the match. Page B15.

Australian high jumper Tim Forsyth is a likely medal contender after reaching the final in the World Athletic Championships in Athens. Several favourites for the event have not made the final, but Forsyth had qualified for the next round with his first jump. Page B15.
THE HERALD SUN

Hawthorn Australian Football League coach Ken Judge says a number of senior players at the club may be sacked for their contributions to the club's bad season. Judge believe various players have performed poorly since the State of Origin match in June. Pge 72.

Three Australian tennis players are in the third round of play at the ATP Tournament in Mason, Ohio. Todd Woodbridge, Mark Woodforde and Pat Rafter advanced yesterday, with Woodbridge eliminating compatriot Jason Stoltenberg. Page 63.

The Australian cricket team will check the fitness of captain Mark Taylor before finalising on the team for the fifth Test match starting tomorrow. Leading England pace bowler Darren Gough is also in doubt for the match due to injury. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

New South Wales cricket captain Greg Matthews is likely to be replaced as captain for the upcoming season. Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor is the likely replacement for Matthews, even though he will be absent for numerous matches through representative commitments. Page 74.

Australian spin bowler Shane Warne may play for an English county cricket team next year if he receives the approval of the Australian Cricket Board. Warne has received a large offer from Sussex to play a shortened season between Australian commitments. page 74.

The Brisbane Broncos Super League team finalised their quarter-finals place in the World Challenge by defeating Halifax 54-10 in England. Broncos centre Steve Renouf was the star, scoring four tries in a comprehensive victory. Page 71.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
